title: Without form
hookLine: names that say devotion wins her, then names that say she is without form
carry: saguna and nirguna: near, and beyond form
tomorrow: who wrote the thousand names, and who may say them?
last: FROM THE ROOT TO THE CROWN.

cards: Sanskrit has a small prefix, nir, that works a lot like the English word without. Put it in front of a word and the word turns inside out.
In the Lalita Sahasranama there's a stretch where name after name begins that way: without support, without stain, without form. What makes the run startling is what comes just before it.
A few names earlier, the hymn has been saying the warmest things about her: how close she is, how easily she's reached.

teach.b: First, the nearness. In paraphrase: she is fond of devotion, reached through devotion, won over by devotion, and she is the one who takes fear away. A goddess you could talk to across a kitchen table.
Then, a little further on, the other run. Without support, needing nothing to stand on. Stainless.
Without qualities, nirguna. Without parts. Peaceful.
Without desire. The hymn that painted her face, her four hands, her throne, now says she has no form at all. Hindu thinkers have names for these two ways of speaking.
Saguna: with qualities, the goddess you can see, praise and love. Nirguna: beyond qualities, the reality no picture can hold. Teachers in different schools weigh the two differently.
Some say the formless is the deeper truth and the forms are a kindness to us. Others say the form is no lesser thing, that she is fully present in it.
The hymn keeps both in the same breath. And notice one name in the run: without desire. Four days ago, desire was the noose in her hand.
The hymn is happy to say both. That fits the week: the mother and the fire, the inner life in her hands, a war that ended in love restored, five acts, a home in the body.
Now no address can hold her. It's also why a Hindu can bow to a small picture on a shelf and, in the same breath, say God has no form. Not a contradiction.
Two true ways of speaking, and the hymn uses both.

how: Devotees reciting the Lalita Sahasranama pass from names that praise her form and her closeness to devotees into names that call her formless and beyond qualities, and different Hindu schools explain the relation of saguna and nirguna in different ways.

o: a hymn listing the temples where Lalita lives
a hymn that names only the goddess's outward form
a hymn naming her both near and beyond all form

games.q: near, and without: tap the pairs.
p: with qualities: the goddess you can see

s: a hymn that describes her face and hands can't also call her formless
the same hymn does both: it paints her form, then names her without form, without parts.
just before the run of without names, the hymn says devotion can win her over
fond of devotion, reached through devotion, won over by devotion.
every Hindu school agrees the formless is the deeper truth
some say so; others say she is fully present in the form. the hymn keeps both.

games.q: you've just recited names that call the goddess fond of devotion, easily reached. what do the next names in the hymn do?
o: describe her jewels in more detail.
turn to names of without: without form, without qualities.
list the gods who serve her.
games.why: a little further on comes the run of nir names: without support, stainless, without form, without qualities, without parts, without desire.

practice: Bring to mind a face, an image or a word that feels close to you, something you could speak to, and let it be near; then gently let the picture go and stay with what's left, the breath, the quiet, the room.

Let the picture come back if it wants to, and move between the two without choosing. If you pray, you can rest with the goddess, or with God, in either way; if you don't, simply notice the difference.

wordCard.voice: The Lalita Sahasranama. Today, names of nearness, won over by devotion, and names of without: without form, without qualities, without parts.

orig.note: Sanskrit nirguṇā: 'without qualities,' one of the names in the hymn's run of nir names.

carryVoice: Your line: saguna and nirguna, near, and beyond form, in the same breath. A week walked.
